objective: Run a bounded cost-sensitivity check for lookback 3/5/10 momentum under the repository's existing realistic cost model and matched null; classify cost robustness.
observed_effect: The cost-sensitivity check is reproducible and independently verified, but its dominant finding is a research-integrity correction rather than a cost number: the admitted 'momentum edge' is not a momentum signal. research/backtest/regime_stability.py::momentum_signals computes mean(log(price)) over the lookback window (always positive for adjusted close > 1) and takes its sign, so it is a constant LONG on every bar independent of lookback; mean_reversion_signals is the same defect with the opposite sign (constant SHORT). Consequences: (1) the prior 'momentum SUPPORTED 7/10 REGIME_STABLE' result is a constant-long equity-beta/drift bet, not a momentum anomaly; (2) the prior 'reversal FALSIFIED' result is a constant-short, and the reported -0.99 momentum/reversal correlation is trivially -1; (3) lookback 3/5/10 'robustness' is vacuous (identical signal at every lookback, hence identical medians). Cost classification: the constant-long candidate is COST_ROBUST 7/10 at all lookbacks (low 3.81x turnover, medians essentially unchanged from zero to 4x cost) because it is beta, not because momentum survives costs; a correctly implemented short-horizon momentum signal (previous lookback-day return, ~105x turnover) shows NO robust positive edge at zero cost (NO_EDGE 10/10 at every lookback) and is cost-fragile where marginally positive.
question: Does the short-horizon momentum edge survive conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected real-data universe?
research_result: VERIFIED NEGATIVE / REFRAMING RESULT. Cost-sensitivity artifact + independent verifier classify cost robustness for lookback 3/5/10. Finding: research/backtest/regime_stability.py::momentum_signals (and ::mean_reversion_signals) do not implement the documented 'previous N-day return' hypothesis; they compute the mean log PRICE, which is always positive for these adjusted-close series, so the signal is a constant long (all 4460 non-neutral bars +1) and the reversal signal a constant short. The previously admitted momentum SUPPORTED (7/10 REGIME_STABLE) and reversal FALSIFIED verdicts therefore describe constant long/short (equity beta / drift), not momentum/reversal; the lookback 3/5/10 robustness is vacuous. On cost: the constant-long candidate is COST_ROBUST 7/10 (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA, JPM) at every lookback (medians ~+0.05..+0.13, essentially unchanged from zero to 4x cost; 3.81x annualized turnover) and NO_EDGE for NVDA/JNJ/XOM; a corrected return-based momentum diagnostic (105x turnover) is NO_EDGE 10/10 at every lookback at zero cost and cost-fragile. Independent verifier: all four gates MATCH (fresh walk_forward+noise_benchmark; cross-consistency vs momentum_lookback_sweep_results.json on all 10 tickers; classification reproducibility; determinism). Primary question answered: the short-horizon momentum edge does not survive cost stress because, as implemented and as corrected, there is no robust short-horizon momentum edge on this universe; the prior positive evidence is an artifact of the signal defect.
uncertainty_reduced: Resolved the primary question decisively: there is no short-horizon momentum edge to survive cost stress. The admitted positive candidate is a constant-long beta bet (verified implementation defect), which is cost-robust only because it is low turnover; the corrected momentum signal has no robust positive edge and is cost-fragile. This also resolves why the prior lookback-robustness result was degenerate and invalidates the per-asset momentum/reversal evidence base pending re-test.
